name: Jeroboam
bio:
Jeroboam son of Nebat was an Ephraimite from Zeredah, son of a widow named Zeruah, and one of Solomon's own officials — a capable, industrious young man whom Solomon had put in charge of all the forced labor of the house of Joseph after noticing his diligence (1 Kings 11:26-28).

One day, as Jeroboam was leaving Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met him alone in a field. Ahijah was wearing a new cloak, and he took it and tore it into twelve pieces, telling Jeroboam to take ten of them: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'See, I am going to tear the kingdom out of Solomon's hand and give you ten tribes.'" Ahijah explained that this judgment came because Solomon had forsaken the LORD to worship Ashtoreth, Chemosh, and Molek, but that for David's sake one tribe would remain with Solomon's son; if Jeroboam obeyed the LORD's commands as David had, the LORD would be with him, build him a dynasty as enduring as David's, and give him Israel (1 Kings 11:29-39). When Solomon heard of this and sought to kill him, Jeroboam fled to Egypt, to King Shishak, and remained there until Solomon's death (1 Kings 11:40). Jeroboam's return from exile and his rise to become the first king of the northern kingdom of Israel, splitting Solomon's kingdom as Ahijah had prophesied, is told in detail in the chapters ahead.
